signature.operations_json: str — JSON array (or single object coerced to one-element array) of operation dicts
signature.returns: str — compact JSON WorkflowResult from common/results.py

allowed_actions.enforcement: run_op raises ValueError('Action not allowlisted: …') if action not in set

ref_grammar.syntax: String values starting with '$' reference a prior step by id
algorithm: If ref does not start with '$', return ref unchanged (literal value)
If step_id not in step_results, raise ValueError('Unknown $ref: …')
If step_results[step_id] has key 'label', return that string
Else if it has key 'path', return that string
Else raise ValueError('$ref … has no label/path')

step_result_shapes.other_actions: do not write step_results unless action defines id

label_aliases.returns: first non-empty string value, or empty string

operations_json.parser: parse_json_list — accepts JSON array or single object (wrapped as one-element list)

limits.behaviour_when_exceeded: Immediate error_result; no ops executed; message 'Batch limit 20 exceeded (N ops)'

mutating_ops_skipped: spawn_actor (records would-spawn warning; still writes step_results[step_id] with label if id present)
still_executes: resolve_actor — NOT guarded by dry_run; always resolves actor
dry_run.warnings: Each skipped op appends a dry_run: … string to warnings list

stop_on_error.invalid_op_not_dict: errors.append('Invalid op: …'); break loop if stop_on_error else continue
stop_on_error.success_field: success = not errors (any error → success false)

transaction.scope: Entire batch in one editor transaction

compile_blueprint.effect: compile_blueprint_paths([path]); compile errors appended to errors list (does not stop unless stop_on_error on exception path — compile errs extend errors but run_op does not raise)

response_shape.step_results_in_response: Full step_results dict returned in extra for agent chaining visibility

disposition.grammar: preserve — $ref-by-step-id, allowlisted actions, dry_run, stop_on_error, BATCH_LIMIT are proven patterns for WS-05 execute_plan schema
disposition.surface: supersede — replace REAgentTools JSON-string tool with ADR-0003 envelope execute_plan action
disposition.implementation: internalise — REAgentTools batch_workflow may remain during migration; hide via SetNameFilters once UEREMCP covers allowlisted ops

relationship_to_epic_execute_tool_script.epic_input: Python script with run() calling execute_tool(dotted_name, json_input)
relationship_to_epic_execute_tool_script.epic_scope: Any registered toolset tool; sandboxed Python; async; editor transaction with undo on failure
relationship_to_epic_execute_tool_script.reagent_scope: 8 fixed RE editor ops; JSON array; sync; ScopedEditorTransaction
relationship_to_epic_execute_tool_script.relationship: compose — do not rebuild execute_tool_script. UEREMCP execute_plan should: (1) adopt REAgentTools $ref/allowlist/dry_run semantics for plan steps; (2) delegate Epic-domain batches (Niagara, Blueprint DSL, etc.) to execute_tool_script steps inside the same plan
relationship_to_epic_execute_tool_script.niagara_pattern: REAgentTools NIAGARA_BATCHING.md uses execute_tool_script for Epic NiagaraToolsets — orthogonal to execute_editor_batch

ws05_recommendations: Plan step id + $stepId.field ref syntax should mirror _resolve_ref (label preferred, path fallback)
Keep allowlist extensibility — REAgentTools frozenset is minimal; UEREMCP plan should reference domain action schemas not raw editor subs
Preserve dry_run default false, stop_on_error default true
BATCH_LIMIT 20 is a tuned default — consider making configurable per security tier (WS-12)
Plan steps wrapping Epic tools should use execute_tool_script composition, not reimplement sandbox
